source.title: From Text to Space: Mapping Abstract Spatial Models in LLMs during a Grid-World Navigation Task

record.tranche_reason: The study probes individual units for shared spatial features across prompt representations and a separate task, refining the interpretation of unit selectivity. It does not directly test whether the same units respond to unrelated non-spatial features.
record.gate_note: Rows record unit-level results relevant to the shared-feature interpretation in V6. The study's navigation success rates and ablations are not included as rows: they do not measure whether individual units respond to unrelated features. The authors' statement that wider spatial representations are likely polysemantic is an interpretation, not a direct measurement of mixed unrelated responses.
record.test_reason: The study probes LLaMA-3.1-8B hidden-state units for correlations with spatial features (agent x/y, border, action correctness) across six prompt formats and a separate spatial-question task. It never measures whether a unit responds to unrelated inputs, how many neurons are polysemantic, or whether apparent polysemantic neurons reduce to one shared feature. Its units are per-layer hidden-state dimensions, not MLP neurons. 'Polysemantic' appears only as a speculative interpretation of why large ablations break output and why core units may not be monosemantic. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. One correction: the polysemantic-neuron remarks are speculation. The authors guess that the wide SIR-specific representation is 'likely comprised mostly of polysemantic neurons' because ablating 59.7% of parameters broke output. They also note that core units 'might not be monosemantic'. Neither remark is measured.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear regression and per-unit correlation probes, cross-representation comparisons, and an unrelated-task activation comparison; it does not use the original sources' feature-visualization or sparse-feature methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The number and distribution of units depended on the feature being probed and the cross-representation threshold (all six versus at least five SIR types). Spatial activation generalization to the separate task was observed for action-correctness units but not for agent-position units.

fits_no_version.finding: Subsets of LLaMA-3.1-8B hidden units correlate with agent x/y position, border status and action correctness across all six prompt formats, well above shuffled controls. Action-correctness units are also more active on unrelated spatial questions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLMs contain format-invariant abstract spatial units, concentrated in middle layers.

record.problems: The internal-unit analysis is limited to LLaMA-3.1-8B. The separate-task comparison contrasts spatial with non-spatial questions but does not test unrelated features within the same individual units. Several unit counts are compared with shuffled controls without exact shuffled counts stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Ablation outcomes (55% success after silencing core action-correctness units versus 59% intact; 62% after silencing core position units) and loss of coherent output after ablating 59.7% of parameters are not included because they measure task performance or output coherence, not whether individual units respond to unrelated features. See Section 6 and Appendix B.3.

untested.parts: No count or share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts.
No analysis of initialization, regularization or noise.
No comparison across architectures, activation functions or regularization.
No reexamination of canonical polysemantic neurons; no test of whether the units' responses are unrelated mixtures.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 labels should be dropped. Activation for spatial vs non-spatial questions does not show shared-feature versus unrelated-mixture coding. The units are residual hidden-state dimensions, not MLP neurons.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons and the cited InceptionV1 example.
The study does not measure a share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts in language models.
No test of superposition or capacity pressure.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization methods for polysemanticity.

The study finds units associated with shared spatial features across formats and tasks, but does not test whether the same units respond to unrelated non-spatial features, nor whether truly unrelated mixtures are rare generally.
No comparison of activation-range choices or explanation-scoring methods for classifying polysemanticity.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual-unit activation correlations with agent x-position separately for each representation and identified units significant across all six SIR types.
rows.measure: Number of units significantly correlated with agent x-position across all SIR types
rows.baseline: Shuffling parameter indices between SIR types markedly reduced the number; exact shuffled count not stated.
rows.note: The units were predominantly in intermediate and deeper layers.
rows.check: Measures cross-format selectivity for agent x-position, not response to unrelated features; bears on no version. The paper's text cites Fig. 4, but the plot is in Fig. 3 (bottom panels).

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual-unit activation correlations with agent y-coordinate separately for each representation and identified units significant across all six SIR types.
rows.measure: Number of units significantly correlated with agent y-coordinate across all SIR types
rows.baseline: Shuffling parameter indices between SIR types markedly reduced the number; exact shuffled count not stated.
rows.note: These units tended to be concentrated in superficial layers.
rows.check: Cross-format y-coordinate selectivity; not a polysemanticity measure. The figure is Fig. 3, not Fig. 4.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual-unit activation correlations with whether the agent was on a border cell and identified units significant across all six SIR types.

conditions.value: agent located on a grid-border cell

rows.measure: Number of units significantly correlated with border-cell status across all SIR types
rows.baseline: Shuffled control; exact count not stated.
rows.note: The invariant units were primarily concentrated in approximately layers 8–18.
rows.check: Cross-format border-cell selectivity; not a polysemanticity measure. The figure is Fig. 3, not Fig. 4.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual-unit activation correlations with action correctness and identified units significant across all six SIR types.

conditions.value: whether the selected action moves the agent closer to the goal

rows.measure: Number of units significantly correlated with action correctness across all SIR types
rows.note: The units were predominantly in approximately layers 12–22.
rows.check: Action-correctness units across formats (286 vs 12 shuffled); this concerns spatial generality, not mixed or unrelated responses.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the action-correctness unit analysis with a threshold of significance in at least five of the six representations.

conditions.value: significant in at least five of six SIR types

rows.measure: Number and layer distribution of units meeting the relaxed cross-representation criterion
rows.baseline: Shuffled control; exact count not stated.
rows.value: 1,560 units; more common units than expected by chance
rows.note: The units remained concentrated in middle layers, with almost none in earlier layers.
rows.check: Relaxed-threshold count; not a polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the correlation between average activation of the 286 core action-correctness units and whether a question was spatial, using a separate spatial/non-spatial reasoning task.

conditions.value: 286 units significant for action correctness across all six SIR types

rows.measure: Distribution of per-unit correlations between average activation and spatial-question status
rows.value: Correlation distribution significantly higher than zero
rows.note: The separate questions involved spatial reasoning outside the grid-world task; the result indicates greater activation for spatial than non-spatial questions, not responses to unrelated features within individual units.
rows.check: Shows that core units are more active on spatial questions. It does not test whether the same units respond to unrelated non-spatial features, so it cannot bear on V6.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the same spatial-question activation correlation for randomly selected units matched to the core units per layer.

conditions.value: random units, matched in number per layer to the 286 core units

rows.measure: Correlation between average activation and spatial-question status
rows.value: No significant bias toward spatial questions
rows.check: Random-unit control for R6; not linked to any version.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured spatial-question activation correlations for core units identified as encoding agent position across all SIR types.
rows.measure: Correlation between average activation and spatial-question status
rows.value: Correlations were not significantly higher than zero
rows.note: Unlike the action-correctness units in R6, these units did not show a detectable association with the spatial nature of the separate questions.
rows.check: Position units show no spatial-question bias; not a polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Looked for units correlated with the same specific grid cell across every SIR type.

conditions.value: agent occupying a particular grid cell

rows.measure: Presence of any unit consistently correlated with the same grid cell across all SIR types
rows.note: The authors contrast this with the cross-representation units encoding x/y coordinates and border status.
rows.check: No unit tracks the same grid cell across formats; this is about place-cell-like coding, not polysemanticity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Core action-correctness units across all six representations and the separate spatial/non-spatial question task
reader_labels.reason: The same 286 units were associated with action correctness across formats and had greater activation for spatial than non-spatial questions, consistent with a shared spatial function rather than evidence of unrelated mixtures (R4, R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Agent-position units and the shared specific-grid-cell test
reader_labels.reason: Core position units did not show a significant spatial-question association, and no unit tracked the same specific grid cell across all representations; the shared-feature pattern is therefore feature-dependent (R8, R9).
